name: Twilight Lavender
lede: Twilight Lavender is a dusty, reddish purple named for the fading evening sky rather than the [[lavender]] flower directly.

sections.title: A sky word, not a flower
sections.body:
Our library traces the name only to a Wikipedia color list, which gives no date for when it entered use [1]. Despite carrying lavender in its name, the word twilight points to the sky at dusk, so the color is filed as a landscape word rather than a plant one [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[dull-magenta-purple]], 3.0 units of CIEDE2000 away and described as almost the same [2]. [[raisin-purple]] sits at 3.4, also almost the same, [[corinthian-purple]] at 3.5, redder and duller, and [[dull-dark-purple]] at 3.9, purpler [2]. Measured in LCH it reads lightness 40, chroma 33, a dark, moderately saturated reddish purple [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in just 9 of 23,781 paintings (0.04 percent), rarer than 78 percent of the named colors, as photographed [3]. The earliest dated match is 1600, though the archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor and not a first [3]. The latest dated match is 1915, across 8 dated paintings in total [3]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, so a color match is not a pigment test [3].
